vendors.name: Old Marta
vendors.greeting: New recruits always need more than the valley gives them. I try to fill the gap.

vendors.name: Kelm the Merchant
vendors.greeting: Potions, supplies, the usual. Prices go up past Razor Hill, so stock up here.

vendors.name: Shu the Sage
vendors.greeting: The islands provide much, but some things must be bought.

vendors.name: Gruk the Supplier
vendors.greeting: Far from the city, but I keep the essentials.

vendors.name: Tarhek the Provisioner
vendors.greeting: Everything a traveler needs, all under one roof.

vendors.name: Mishka Emberflask
vendors.greeting: Vials, reagents, and the potions you can't brew yet — that's my trade.

vendors.name: Grima Saltbrand
vendors.greeting: Small trade post. Take what you need.

vendors.name: Gazlowe's Cousin Nixx
vendors.greeting: Ratchet moves goods. I'm part of that.

vendors.name: Dockmaster Brindle
vendors.greeting: Ships need a dockmaster. Dockmaster needs a drink.

vendors.name: Hela Windhoof
vendors.greeting: Taurajo runs lean. What you see is what we've got.

vendors.name: Zeppelin Master Snurk
vendors.greeting: Long flights, short supplies. Stock up before you board.

vendors.name: Undertaker Mordo
vendors.greeting: The Forsaken require supplies like any living thing. Mostly.

vendors.name: Innkeeper Renee
vendors.greeting: Rest your feet. I'll have food on the table.

vendors.name: Vrakk Thundertusk
vendors.greeting: If you make things, I sell what goes into them.

vendors.name: Kagra Ironbind
vendors.greeting: Good steel needs good flux. I sell both.

vendors.name: Stablemaster Grosh
vendors.greeting: The mounts eat well. You should too.

vendors.name: Fizzwick Trueshot
vendors.greeting: String, feathers, resin — everything that turns a plank into a bow.

vendors.name: Trader Bloodhorn
vendors.greeting: Hides come in, leather goes out. I sell what helps the middle part.

vendors.name: Grainkeeper Yura
vendors.greeting: The plains provide the meat. I do the cooking.

vendors.name: Spiritcarver Dennok
vendors.greeting: Spirits require preparation. So do adventurers.

vendors.name: Beastcaller Nira
vendors.greeting: Beasts and their trainers both need keeping.

vendors.name: Trader Fennimore
vendors.greeting: A little of everything. That's Brill for you.

vendors.name: Silas Grimme
vendors.greeting: Mages and warlocks keep me busy. I don't ask why.

vendors.name: Butcher Hollane
vendors.greeting: Fresh cuts, cured meats, and something to wash it down.

vendors.name: Seamstress Vance
vendors.greeting: Thread, dye, and the knowledge to use them. The garments are your business.

vendors.name: Curio Merchant Fenn
vendors.greeting: Old things, new uses. That's the Forsaken way.

vendors.name: Apothecary Wrenn
vendors.greeting: The arcane requires discipline. And proper vials.

vendors.name: Innkeeper Doss
vendors.greeting: The Sepulcher's cold, but my hearth isn't.

vendors.name: Mortician Grieve
vendors.greeting: Preservation is an art. Salt is its foundation.

vendors.name: Cargo Master Blix
vendors.greeting: I ship what others can't source locally.

vendors.name: Fuzzek Boomwick
vendors.greeting: Explosives, elixirs — close enough business.

vendors.name: The Fence
vendors.greeting: What you're looking for isn't on the shelf. That's why you came to me.

vendors.name: Tavern Keeper Molka
vendors.greeting: Sit down. I'll get you something.

vendors.name: Ulvara Deepwind
vendors.greeting: Reagents for every school. I don't play favorites.

vendors.name: Trask Beastcaller
vendors.greeting: Beasts of Durotar, fed and cared for.

vendors.name: Quartermaster Grosh
vendors.greeting: The Horde marches on full bellies and sharp steel.

vendors.name: Karnessa Voidsight
vendors.greeting: The Burning Blade has its needs. I supply them — no questions.

vendors.name: Snizzle Boltcrank
vendors.greeting: Good machines start with good materials.

vendors.name: Scout Windrider
vendors.greeting: Light, fast, prepared. That's a good scout.

vendors.name: Grukk Ironhide
vendors.greeting: Orgrimmar eats well. I make sure of it.

vendors.name: Zeeka Bloodfang
vendors.greeting: Pre-brewed and ready. Saves you the vials.

vendors.name: Provisioner Hemma Redbrand
vendors.greeting: Southern Barrens waypost. We carry what fits in a saddle bag.

vendors.name: Quartermaster Gruzk Ironhide
vendors.greeting: Northern Barrens basecamp. Moving fast — grab what you need.

vendors.name: Fishmonger Sylra
vendors.greeting: Remote post. I trade what washes up and what I haul in.

vendors.name: Zeppelin Master Grub
vendors.greeting: The zeppelin waits for no one. Least of all the unprepared.

vendors.name: Innkeeper Nethra
vendors.greeting: The Undercity doesn't sleep. Neither do I.

vendors.name: Quartermaster Dolan
vendors.greeting: The Dark Lady's forces demand the best. I provide it.

vendors.name: Provisioner Nell
vendors.greeting: Provisioning the dead is still provisioning.

vendors.name: Arcanist Welsh
vendors.greeting: The Undercity breeds scholars. I supply them.

vendors.name: Imp-Keeper Zalnak
vendors.greeting: We don't discuss where these come from.

vendors.name: Elixir Dealer Quill
vendors.greeting: Every soldier needs an edge. I sell them.

vendors.name: Reagent Dealer Hollis
vendors.greeting: The craft guilds send me their shopping lists.

vendors.name: Poisoner Sable
vendors.greeting: Assassination is a craft. I supply the materials.

vendors.name: Quartermaster Brask
vendors.greeting: Silverpine is dangerous. Come prepared.

vendors.name: Quartermaster Vorn
vendors.greeting: Southern Silverpine post. The wolves don't wait.

vendors.name: Provisioner Dunn
vendors.greeting: Fenris Isle doesn't get many supply ships. Make it count.

vendors.name: Innkeeper Mallory Dunn
vendors.greeting: Room's yours if you want it. I'll not ask which bank you came off.

vendors.name: Goodwife Serrin Holt
vendors.greeting: Flour, thread, lamp oil. Whatever the mill does not eat, I sell.

vendors.name: Smith Odrin Vance
vendors.greeting: I shoe their horses and mend their cart axles. A trade is a trade.

vendors.name: Bowyer Tess Aldren
vendors.greeting: Yew from the river stand, strung the way my father strung them.

vendors.name: Factor Vell
vendors.greeting: The Society requisitions. I merely keep the ledger, and the ledger keeps everyone honest.

vendors.name: Apothecary Lysbet Crane
vendors.greeting: Mind the vats. What is in them is not finished, and it does not like being looked at.

vendors.name: Vat-Tender Grusk
vendors.greeting: Stir it, skim it, log it. Twelve years dead and I have a trade again.

vendors.name: Quartermaster Dreng
vendors.greeting: Tower stores. Signed for, counted twice, and I will know if it is not.

vendors.name: Quartermaster Ivek
vendors.greeting: A forward post gets forward-post stock. Do not ask for anything polished.

vendors.name: Quartermaster Sule
vendors.greeting: Gate stores. The town has its own shops across the bridges; this is for people who are leaving.

vendors.name: Quartermaster Sylvaine
vendors.greeting: Everything here was carried down a fissure on somebody's back. Price it accordingly.

vendors.name: Factor Anselm Dawnmere
vendors.greeting: I trade in two directions and only one of them goes up the fissure. Guess which has the margin.

vendors.name: Smith Harvald Emberlock
vendors.greeting: No coal down here worth the name. I burn what the Codex rules is expendable, and they rule often.

vendors.name: Reagent-Keeper Ilthea
vendors.greeting: Catalogued, labelled, shelved. If you want it unlabelled, go and pull it out of the ground yourself.

vendors.name: Innkeeper Maeven Sorrowglass
vendors.greeting: There is no night here. We decided there was one anyway, and I keep the hours. Somebody has to.

vendors.name: Alchemist Terrowen
vendors.greeting: Four years of samples and the reagents keep testing BETTER than their surface equivalents. I have stopped putting that in reports.

vendors.name: Campkeeper Threnn
vendors.greeting: Last supplies before the Geode. I am required to tell you that and required not to tell you why.

vendors.name: Cook Behr Ashmantle
vendors.greeting: Everything here gets smoked because everything here gets wet. You will stop minding the taste.

vendors.name: Smith Durga Ironhoof
vendors.greeting: No ore in this mountain worth the walk. I mend what comes up the trail and I charge for the mending, not the metal.

vendors.name: Quartermaster Bren Hollowhorn
vendors.greeting: Everything on these shelves came up a ramp on somebody's back. The price reflects the back.

vendors.name: Cook Dorn Steadyhand
vendors.greeting: Up here the fire wants watching. Wind takes the heat sideways and your supper with it.

vendors.name: Warehouse-Keeper Dral
vendors.greeting: If it came up the ramp this season, I know where it is. If it did not, stop asking me about it.

vendors.name: Tally-Clerk Nessa
vendors.greeting: Everything that crosses this top gets written down. It is not suspicion. It is that we lost a city once without a list of what was in it.

vendors.name: Herb-Seller Winn
vendors.greeting: Mesa herbs, aspen herbs and whatever the caravans bring. Three climates on one table, which is not something any herbalist before me had to price.

vendors.name: Hide-Trader Molk
vendors.greeting: Mountain hides from the north, mesa hides from below. The northern ones are thicker and nobody has worked out what to do with that yet.

vendors.name: Spice-Trader Ovi
vendors.greeting: Salt from the flats, east of here. It is the one trade the Integration did not touch, and I have never been so glad to be boring.

vendors.name: Relic-Keeper Dun
vendors.greeting: Things that came up out of the mesas and things that came down off the mountain. I can tell you which is which. I cannot always tell you what either one is.

vendors.name: Smith Durga Ironhoof
vendors.greeting: Ore comes up the ramp in sacks and the charcoal comes up behind it. I forge the most expensive horseshoes on the continent and everybody here needs them.

vendors.name: Weaponsmith Karr
vendors.greeting: Three years ago I made tools. I would like to go back to making tools and I am not going to.

vendors.name: Reagent-Keeper Ulla
vendors.greeting: Spirit-work needs its materials and the spirits up here are not the ones we knew. Different herbs. Different smoke. Same asking.

vendors.name: Pell Dunewright
vendors.greeting: Nobody comes down this gully by accident, so I'll assume you want something.

vendors.name: Hesta Coldhand
vendors.greeting: I came down here to look at the ice. Staying was a separate decision.

vendors.name: Veln Ashgrease
vendors.greeting: You didn't see me and I didn't see what you're carrying. Now, business.

vendors.name: Quill Lampwright
vendors.greeting: Down here you buy what you need before you need it. Nobody comes back up for a second trip.

vendors.name: Quartermaster Ghal
vendors.greeting: Signed for, issued, and I want it back.

vendors.name: Trader Burg
vendors.greeting: Whatever came up the stair this week, I have some of it.

vendors.name: Provisioner Nakka
vendors.greeting: Eat before you go south. People forget.

vendors.name: Weaponsmith Trag
vendors.greeting: Oil it every night down here or it will not be yours by morning.

vendors.name: Herbalist Mossa
vendors.greeting: Half of what grows out there will kill you. I sell the other half.

vendors.name: Trader Nixxle
vendors.greeting: Everything on this shelf came off a boat that was going somewhere else.

vendors.name: Keeper Marla
vendors.greeting: Drink it inside. What you spill out there, the tide keeps.

vendors.name: Clerk Bexx
vendors.greeting: Manifest, weight, destination. In that order or not at all.

vendors.name: Gurgle
vendors.greeting: Caught this morning. Some of it caught itself.

vendors.name: Dealer Sark
vendors.greeting: I do not ask what for. I do ask for coin first.

vendors.name: Innkeeper Vozzi Rimehand
vendors.greeting:
Bed, board, and a bind. That is the full list and I will not be upsold on your behalf.

Before you ask: there is no wind rider. There was never a wind rider. You came in on your feet and that is how you are leaving, so eat something.

vendors.name: Trader Grebbit Maul
vendors.greeting: Everything on this table came across the pan on a cart with four bad wheels. The price is the wheels. It was always the wheels.

vendors.name: Brewer Nissa Tolk
vendors.greeting: Salt air ruins a cork in a season, so I seal everything in lead and I charge you for the lead. Yes, I have heard what they say about lead. Drink it fast.

vendors.name: Jixa Brinecount
vendors.greeting:
Salt. That is it, that is the whole business, and it is the only trade on this pan that the Integration did not touch.

Everybody laughed at me for twenty years. They are not laughing now, they are just gone.

vendors.name: Road-Agent Fenk Dustle
vendors.greeting:
I sell what you need to walk out of here, which is a thriving business, because walking out of here is the only option available to you.

No bird. Do not go looking for the post. There is a post. There has never been a bird on it.

vendors.name: Quartermaster Dral Wexx
vendors.greeting: Raceday stock. We laid in eight seasons of it the year before the track died, so you are buying from a warehouse that was built for a crowd that is not coming.

vendors.name: Mechanic Oyla Spannerwick
vendors.greeting:
Three years ago a human drove an Earth machine down that straight and it did the whole run on a thimble of fuel and no boiler at all.

I have taken one apart since. I understand it now. That is worse.

vendors.name: Fuel-Trader Mozz
vendors.greeting: I have fuel for two hundred racers and six customers. Do the arithmetic and then make me an offer, because I have done the arithmetic and I am desperate.

vendors.name: Salvager Pim Gattle
vendors.greeting: Everything out on that track is mine the day it stops moving. That is the rule, it is written down, and it has made me the richest wreck-picker on a pan with no wrecks left.

vendors.name: Armourer Hett Grindle
vendors.greeting: Salt gets into a hinge and it is finished. I can slow it. I cannot stop it, and anyone who tells you they can stop it is selling you grease.

vendors.name: Innkeeper Mirabel Sump
vendors.greeting:
Beds upstairs, board down here, and the hearth is yours the moment you touch it.

I have forty beds and I have had forty beds since my mother ran this house. The town has twice the people it did three years ago and I have forty beds, so do the arithmetic and take the one at the end before somebody off the yard does.

vendors.name: Fishmonger Oda Brack
vendors.greeting:
Everything on this slab came out of that water this morning and everything on it will be gone by noon.

I buy my salt off a woman on the pan who has never once been late in eleven years. Her town is dying and my town is not and she still gets the cart out. That is the whole trade, really. Someone keeps turning up.

vendors.name: Chandler Vex Tarrow
vendors.greeting:
Rope, pitch, canvas, lamp oil, and whatever else stops a ship coming apart.

My grandfather chandlered this quay and his father before him, and I will tell you what has changed: nothing, at this counter. Everything, forty yards that way.

vendors.name: Shipwright Hald Keelmaker
vendors.greeting:
A hull does one of two things out here. It gets looked after or it gets burned to the waterline for its nails.

I have had more work in three years than in the twenty before them, and every job of it has come off that yard, and I am not going to pretend that is a coincidence or that I resent it.

vendors.name: Strongbox-Keeper Pell
vendors.greeting:
I hold what people do not want to carry and I write down what they do not want to forget.

There is more in this house than there has ever been and most of it belongs to people who walked here with nothing. You can take that as a sermon or as a fact. It is a fact.

vendors.name: Trader Bix Rannow
vendors.greeting:
Everything, roughly, and if I do not have it I know who does and I will take a cut of telling you.

I had a shop with a stone front and a name cut into the lintel. It is standing in a walled town with nobody in it four days west. This is a shed. The shed makes more money and I would still rather have the lintel.

vendors.name: Smith Dorga Ironside
vendors.greeting:
Hot work, and it is hot already, so I start before the sun does and stop when it is overhead.

Everything I make here goes onto a ship or into the desert, and the two of them want opposite things from a piece of steel. Salt air or dry sand. Pick one and I will temper for it.

vendors.name: Engineer Faz Quill
vendors.greeting:
I build things that mostly work and I am honest about the mostly, which in this trade makes me a radical.

My whole workshop came out of Gadgetzan on three carts. Everything heavier than a cart is still in it. There is a press in that town I think about more than I think about most people.

vendors.name: Brewer Tansy Vohl
vendors.greeting:
Sealed against sea air, which is a different problem from sealed against dry air and costs more.

There is a woman out on the pan who seals in lead for the same reason and charges less. She also has six customers. I have four hundred. Neither of us is doing it wrong.

vendors.name: Broker Nim Catchpenny
vendors.greeting:
I buy what came off something and sell it to whoever needs it on something else.

Half of what crosses this counter came out of Gadgetzan and I will not pretend otherwise. If that bothers you, it is still for sale.

vendors.name: Agent Rullo Tack
vendors.greeting:
Freight west, freight south, and a price for each that assumes you have looked at the alternatives.

There is a pan north of here with a town on it that has wanted a regular cart for three years. I could run one. I have not, and the reason is not the hives, it is that there is nothing coming back the other way worth the axle.

vendors.name: Cook Brodd Kettlewick
vendors.greeting:
Welcome to the Kettle. It was my cook tent until the dig stopped. Then people kept sleeping in it, so the crew put up walls and now it's an inn.

There's stew on and there are real beds upstairs. If you want to bind your hearth here, say so. It saves you the walk down the ramp next time.

vendors.name: Quartermaster Dez Hobbin
vendors.greeting:
Everything the dig still owns, and the dig has not dug anything in eleven months.

This camp was provisioned for ninety people. There are ten of us. So I am generous with the rope and I am generous with the lamp oil and I will remain generous right up until somebody from the Survey asks me for a favour.

vendors.name: Cutter Vessa Quill
vendors.greeting:
Vein glass. Cut, backed, and set into whatever you are already wearing.

There is one seam in the world that shrugs off a spell and you are standing in the hole it came out of. I have about four months of cut stock left. After that I am a very skilled woman sitting on a rock, so you will understand why I have a view about reopening the works.

vendors.name: Brewer Nix Pallow
vendors.greeting:
Brewed with the only clean water for a hundred miles, which is the single best thing about this posting.

Everybody up top pays four silver a skin for water hauled from here. I stand in it. Do you know what that does to a man's sense of what things are worth? I have stopped being able to price anything.

vendors.name: Smith Harla Benttooth
vendors.greeting:
Bring it to me before it breaks, not after. Down here after is a long walk.

I repaired pump housings for two years and I have repaired weapons for one, and I will tell you which of those I would rather be doing. A pump that fails floods a gallery. A sword that fails kills the person holding it, and lately the person holding it is somebody I know.

vendors.name: Quartermaster Tobbit Lund
vendors.greeting:
I stock what a camp needs, as long as it fits on four carts.

Four carts is what we can pack and move in a day. We've had to do that twice. I was glad of the rule both times, and I was the only one.

vendors.name: Cook Marda Pell
vendors.greeting:
There are bedrolls under the awning and the pot's on. You get both with the posting.

I've fed this camp in four places and the food's got better each time. It took me a while to learn what a desert has to eat. There isn't much, but I know all of it now.

vendors.name: Smith Gorra Blacktooth
vendors.greeting:
Bring me your gear before it breaks. There's no other forge between here and the port.

I shod kodo for nine years and there's nothing to shoe out here. These days I make peg irons and chain, and I mend whatever the crawlers have chewed.

vendors.name: Brewer Sepp Narrow
vendors.greeting:
I mix everything thin, so the bottles survive the cart.

I came out with the second camp on a three-month contract. That was two years and two camps ago. Nobody's mentioned the contract since, and I haven't either.

vendors.name: Sentinel Weaponsmith
vendors.greeting: Sentinel issue. It is maintained, it is sharp, and I will know if you neglect it.

vendors.name: Astranaar Outfitter
vendors.greeting: Everything here is cut for someone who has to move in it. Try it before you buy it.

vendors.name: Provisioner Shaldrissa
vendors.greeting: Food, water, and something for the pain. In that order, usually.

vendors.name: Quartermaster Huln
vendors.greeting: The Overseer signs for it, you carry it, and it comes back in one piece. That is the arrangement.

vendors.name: Cook Grishna
vendors.greeting: Eat before you go out. I am not sending anybody into that forest hungry.

vendors.name: Supplier Vokk
vendors.greeting: Rope, thread, flux, parchment. Unglamorous, and you will be back for all four.

vendors.name: Quartermaster Horg
vendors.greeting: Camp stores. I requisition for a garrison of forty and I am supplied for a garrison of twelve, so take what you need and do not take more.

vendors.name: Innkeeper Mura Flint
vendors.greeting: There is a roof in the north corner that has held three winters. That is the inn. Set your hearth by the fire and I will not ask you anything else.

vendors.name: Wind Rider Keeper Sharzak
vendors.greeting: Two wyverns. One of them will take you to Hammerfall and one of them will take you to Tarren Mill, and which is which changes depending on their mood.

vendors.name: Quartermaster Urga Ironhand
vendors.greeting: The hold's stores, and the hold's stores are good, because we have been here long enough to build shelves.

vendors.name: Innkeeper Grettha
vendors.greeting: A real inn, with a real fire, and I will tell anyone in Orgrimmar who asks that we built it before the second watchtower and we were right to.

vendors.name: Wind Rider Master Dreka
vendors.greeting: The roost is full and the routes are flown. Hammerfall is on the map now, whatever Orgrimmar's cartographers are still printing.

vendors.name: Weaponsmith Krol Anvilbrand
vendors.greeting: War forge. Not a camp fire with a rock next to it - a forge, with a chimney, built by someone who knew what they were doing. Me.

vendors.name: Trader Molg
vendors.greeting: Everything a soldier forgets to pack and then needs on the moor at four in the afternoon. I have made a study of it.

vendors.name: Reagent-Keeper Shelna
vendors.greeting: Components. Measured, labelled and dated, because the alternative is Apothecary Voss guessing, and he has guessed before.

vendors.name: Herbalist Nahto Greenhoof
vendors.greeting: There is good growing in the basin and nobody here is looking at it. They are all looking at the ogres. The ogres will still be there next season. So will the plants, if somebody tends them.

vendors.name: Quartermaster Dreg
vendors.greeting: Landed stores. Everything here came off a boat and some of it came off somebody else's boat, and I am not going to pretend otherwise.

vendors.name: Salvager Pik Bronzewhistle
vendors.greeting: Six wrecks on the flats and the tide only lets you at them twice a day. I know which two. That knowledge is the business.

vendors.name: Innkeeper Vara Dunn
vendors.greeting: One room, four bunks and a fire that works. It is an inn because I say it is an inn and because there is nowhere else on this coast to say it about.

vendors.name: Wind Rider Keeper Ozra
vendors.greeting: One wyvern, one route, straight back to Hammerfall. If you want to go anywhere else from here you are going by water, and the water out there is Bloodsail.

vendors.name: Innkeeper Brenna Coalcask
vendors.greeting:
Welcome to the Banked Fire. The beds are stone with wool on top and the ale's brewed down here, so it tastes like down here. Most people come round to it by the second mug.

If you want to bind your hearth, say so and I'll set you a place by the fire. It's a long walk back from topside otherwise.

vendors.name: Quartermaster Dolf Ironledger
vendors.greeting:
Company store. Everything on these shelves came down a rope or out of the rock, and the rope goods cost more.

Have a look. If you need something I don't stock, tell me and I'll put it on the next order, but the next order is a month out.

vendors.name: Smith Hulda Emberfall
vendors.greeting:
Mind the quench trough, it's hot.

Everything on the rack is dark iron and I made all of it. If you'd rather make your own, the anvil in the yard is open to anyone, and Forgemaster Garrun over at the smeltery teaches. He's hard on beginners but he's fair.

vendors.name: Armorer Thrain Runehammer
vendors.greeting:
Plate and mail, and I'll set a rune in either if you can pay for it.

I don't repair topside armour. I'm not being rude, the steel's too soft to take our rivets. I can sell you something that'll last longer down here.

vendors.name: Shaft-Warden Kelda Deepvein
vendors.greeting:
Sign the board before you go down the head and sign it again when you're back up. I check it every shift, and if a name's missing its second mark I send people looking.

There's dark iron in the sand outside the gate as well, if you'd rather dig there. Nobody here will stop you. Just watch for the hive while your head's down.

vendors.name: Alchemist Sigrun Vialwright
vendors.greeting:
Careful with the blue jars, they stain.

Most of what I brew starts as mushrooms from the Lantern Wood. The young caps are the good ones, before they open. I pay for them, if you're heading out that way. Nobody else in town will go.

vendors.name: Powderman Brokk Shortfuse
vendors.greeting:
You can stand closer than that. If I thought any of this was going off I wouldn't be sat on it.

Blasting charges for the mine, mostly. The small ones are for the hive. They dig up into our tunnels a few times a year and a charge down the hole is quicker than arguing.

vendors.name: Quartermaster Durn Slagbelt
vendors.greeting:
I keep the landing's stores. Everything on these shelves was carried up from the jetty by hand, so it costs a bit more than on the mainland.

I kept the stores for a mining company for thirty years before the Thane asked me to come out here.

vendors.name: Cook Halla Brinepot
vendors.greeting:
There's food in the pot and bedrolls in the long tent, and you're welcome to both.

The supply boat mostly brings flour and salt, so a lot of what I cook comes out of the shallows to the east. I hope you like crab.

vendors.name: Factor Grib Tallyman
vendors.greeting:
Every cart of ore that goes through this gate gets weighed, and I'm the one who weighs it.

Cinderwharf is through the arch. I keep a few supplies for people heading out to the Works, because it's a long walk.

vendors.name: Quartermaster Vela Coalwright
vendors.greeting:
The front shelf is for anyone with coin. What's behind me is for people the Ashclaim trusts.

You earn that trust by working for the Thane or the Underwriter. I don't mind which.

vendors.name: Smith Hogar Deepvein
vendors.greeting:
I work plate and mail, made from ore that came up through the old city's gate.

The forge behind me is yours to use if you know the trade. If you want leather, try the goblins down by the water.

vendors.name: Armoursmith Brenna Stonecast
vendors.greeting:
Everything I make is forged from Khaz Varun's own iron.

My grandmother was an armoursmith in the old city. Her work is still down there somewhere, and I'd like to see a piece of it one day.

vendors.name: Innkeeper Dolla Pinchspark
vendors.greeting:
Welcome to the Tapped Vein. The dwarves sit on the left and my lot sit on the right.

The middle table is where the contracts get signed. Beds are upstairs, and the stew is whatever came in on the last boat.

vendors.name: Trader Gex Sootpocket
vendors.greeting:
I sell blasting charges, glue, resin and parchment.

I'd rather you didn't ask where my powder comes from. The Thane's people don't like it, so I keep the hatch shut when they walk past.

vendors.name: Alchemist Pell Fizzlewick
vendors.greeting:
I sell potions, vials and a few recipes, including one for a fire ward that you'll want in the Emberdeep.

The yellow crust round the fissures is worth more than the ore. I'd be grateful if you didn't tell the dwarves that.

vendors.name: Broker Tazz Hookfinger
vendors.greeting:
If you've brought anything up out of the old city, I'll buy it, and I pay well.

Dark Iron work sells for a lot on the mainland. The Thane calls it grave robbing.

I also sell leather and cloth supplies, and a couple of patterns for the rugged hides out of the Reach, because nobody else in town bothers.
